anandabas-ten-dome-mosque.desc: This mosque stands in the western para of Anandabas village in Bagoan union, close to Mujibnagar. As the name says, it has ten domes. Of the seven mosques in Anandabas it is the oldest, and locals regard it as the place from which Islam spread in this border area. It is a quiet village stop that fits well into a day at Mujibnagar.
blocks: From Meherpur take a bus or CNG towards Mujibnagar, then an easy-bike to Anandabas village.
Go outside prayer times and ask before entering. The Mujibnagar Memorial is only a few kilometres away.

amjhupi-nilkuthi.desc: Amjhupi Nilkuthi, about six kilometres east of Meherpur town, was built as the house and office of British indigo planters. Its colonnaded rooms and wide lawns run down towards the Kajla river. Local tradition also links the area to the 18th-century politics that preceded the Battle of Plassey. Today it is a pleasant spot for a walk and a lesson in colonial history.
blocks: A short auto ride east from Meherpur town on the Chuadanga road.

ballavpur-mission.desc: Ballavpur has a long-standing Christian community and a mission church that is one of the older ones in the region. The church and its grounds are calm and well kept, surrounded by farmland. Christmas is celebrated here with special services and gatherings. It pairs easily with a visit to Mujibnagar.
blocks: From Mujibnagar, a short auto ride; ask locals for Ballavpur Mission.
Ask permission before entering during services.

bhatpara-nilkuthi.desc: Bhatpara in Gangni holds the ruins of another large indigo factory. Brick buildings and fragments of vats survive among trees. It is less visited than Amjhupi and has a more abandoned feel. Together the two sites show how deeply indigo shaped this border region.
blocks: From Meherpur, take a bus to Gangni and then a van or bike to Bhatpara.
Structures are unstable; look from outside.

mujibnagar-day.desc: Mujibnagar Day marks the swearing-in of the provisional government of Bangladesh in 1971. At the memorial, the day begins with flag raising and guards of honour, followed by a re-enactment of the oath and cultural programmes. Crowds come from across the region. It is the best day to feel the significance of the place.
blocks: Expect security checks and large crowds; arrive early.

glance: 255 km to Meherpur by road, 7–9 hours by bus or car
mujibnagar-memorial.desc: At Baidyanathtala, close to the Indian border, the provisional government of Bangladesh was sworn in on 17 April 1971, and the place was renamed Mujibnagar. A memorial of angled concrete walls now stands in the old mango grove. Nearby, a complex with sculptures and a large map of the war's sectors tells the story. It is a site of national pride and a peaceful green space.
blocks: Bus or auto from Meherpur town (about 30–40 min).
17 April brings large official ceremonies; visit another day for quiet.

glance: Amjhupi mango market and orchards around Meherpur Sadar in June
meherpur-himsagar-mango.desc: About sixty percent of Meherpur's mango orchards are Himsagar, a variety prized for its thick, fibreless, very fragrant flesh. Orchards in Sadar upazila villages such as Jhaubaria and Subidpur supply buyers from Dhaka, Chattogram and Sylhet, and since 2016 some of the crop has been exported to Europe. The harvest peaks from late May through June. Bagged Himsagar, grown in paper bags on the tree, fetches a little more than ordinary fruit.
blocks: Himsagar season is short; go in the first half of June.

meherpur-rosokodom.desc: Rosokodom is a round milk-based sweet whose textured surface is said to resemble a kadam flower. In Meherpur it is sold side by side with sabitri, and both are linked to the town's old sweet makers. It holds up well for travel. Ask for fresh stock in the morning.

glance: Old sweet shops in Meherpur town
meherpur-sabitri.desc: Sabitri is made by slowly boiling milk and sugar down into a firm, fudgy sweet with a deep brown colour. It keeps for days without refrigeration, which made it a favourite gift to carry. Meherpur people consider it their own and send it to relatives elsewhere. The taste is rich and milky, like caramelised khoa.

nigamananda-ashram-kutubpur.desc: Swami Nigamananda Paramahansa, born in 1880 in the village of Kutubpur, then part of Nadia district, grew up here and studied for a while at Meherpur High School. He later became a well-known guru who founded ashrams across Bengal and Assam, including the Saraswat Math at Jorhat. Banglapedia lists the Swami Nigamananda Ashram at Kutubpur among Meherpur Sadar's heritage sites and tourist spots. It makes a calm stop on a day spent around Meherpur's indigo kuthis.
blocks: From Meherpur town take an easy-bike or CNG north to Kutubpur union.
It is a religious place; take off your shoes where asked and dress modestly. Pair it with Amjhupi Nilkuthi.
